newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close moderately higher led by Koor.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close moderately higher led by Koor.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Monday led by a sharp rise in Koor Industries, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares gained 0.29 percent, or 0.86 points, to 295.48 on all-share turnover of 149 million shekels against 115 million shekels on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.38 percent higher at 302.30.
"Activity was dull today and only Koor prevented the market from falling," said Ronen Kaufman of Nesuah Trading and Investments.
Koor, by far the most active share, surged 6.25 percent to 39,146 agorot on volume of 26.9 million shekels amid rumours of further off-the-floor purchases.

The bourse said 257,000 shares were sold off the floor on Sunday for 415 shekels a share, a 15 percent premium to the market price at the time. The block was equal to about two percent of Koor's equity.
Other shares were sold in smaller blocks at 368.43 shekels, the same as Sunday's closing price. All together about $30 million in shares were sold.
"Koor accounted for 0.4 percentage points of the rise in the Maof and if it wasn't for Koor the market would have closed lower," said Idan Azoulay of Impact Union Portfolio Management.
"Activity was low because investors were waiting for the Wall Street opening. They are worried that the Dow will continue to decline," Kaufman said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 130 points on Friday.

Kaufman said the market was also affected by the heavy trading by Maof options speculators. "The Maof players were very active today. Until Thursday (the expiry of the Maof June contracts) the market will remain volatile," he said.

Azoulay added that trading is expected to remain thin until the contracts expiry. "The mood in the market is still very positive but investors are waiting for the expiry before the market can return to behave normally," he said.

Analysts said the market feared options players might dump shares on the market in the run-up to the expiry date in order to lower the index. Azoulay said options players want to see the Maof end at 300 on Thursday.
Once the Maof has ceased to play a role, the market will focus its attentions on inflation. "The fact that the shekel continues to rise gives hope that the next CPI will be relatively low," he said.
Since the release of an unexpectedly high June CPI of 1.1 percent on July 15 the shekel has gained 1.2 percent against the dollar.
Discount Investment Corp lost 1.0 percent to 30,199 agorot. Discount and closely held Paz Oil Co said on Monday they had purchased the Mondex electronic cash franchise rights for Israel.

Other active shares included Bezeq Israel Telecom, which dropped 2.25 percent to 1,003 agorot on turnover of nine million shekels, and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which rose 1.75 percent to 23,095 agorot on volume of 7.8 million shekels.
-- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
